name: Eastern Roman Empire (Justinian I)

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 1.3-1.5 million km2 for 500 CE (East only); adding reconquered Africa (~0.4 million) and Italy (~0.3 million) gives the low. The historical-basemaps world_500 polygons used for the border measure 1.93 (Eastern Roman Empire) + 0.36 (Vandals) + 0.56 (Ostrogoths) = 2.84 million km2 on the sphere, computed from the GeoJSON (mid; they include Provence and Raetia, never recovered). Treadgold's table (isbn:0804726302, p. 278, via the Wikipedia pointer above) has 3.4 million km2 for 565 (high).

population.note: Seshat (East Roman Empire) codes 20 million for 500 CE and 12.5-15 million for 600 CE (East only, before and after). Treadgold, A History of the Byzantine State and Society (isbn:0804726302, p. 278; figures as tabulated at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_of_the_Byzantine_Empire, pointer only) gives 26 million in 540 with Africa and part of Italy, before the plague of 541-542 (high), and 20 million at Justinian's death in 565. Mid 21 million for 555: after the first plague wave, with Italy, Africa and southern Spain now included. Everything inside the border.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Constantinople (Seshat largest settlement 500,000 in 500 CE, https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/72), Alexandria, Antioch and a dense network of Levantine and Anatolian cities; plague and the Persian sack of Antioch (540) cut urban populations. Set below the Principate's 17%.

activePersonnel.note: Field army: Agathias puts the effective army at the end of Justinian's reign, incl. Italy, Africa and Spain, at "barely 150,000" (contemporary; Jones, The Later Roman Empire, https://archive.org/details/JonesLaterRomanEmpire02, pp. 684-685, reads it as the field army excluding the limitanei). Frontier troops: Soto Chica 2015 (https://gladius.revistas.csic.es/index.php/gladius/article/download/277/281/285, p. 71) uses 150,000 field + 100,000 frontier; Treadgold (Byzantium and Its Army, pp. 59-64, 161-162, as summarised at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Roman_army, pointer) gives 150,300 field army + 229,000 frontier troops, guards and oarsmen = 379,300 for 565 (high). Low = Agathias' 150,000 read as the whole army (Bury) + 15,000 oarsmen + guards. Counted: comitatenses, foederati and bucellarii in imperial pay, limitanei (salaried garrison soldiers, though Procopius says Justinian stopped their pay in places), palace guards and the fleet. Allied Lombard, Herul and Ghassanid contingents are in trainedReserves.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Allied and federate contingents called up for campaigns: Ghassanid Arab phylarchs, Lombards and Heruls (5,500 Lombards and 3,000 Heruls served Narses in 552 per Procopius, ancient), Moorish allies in Africa; discharged veterans.

supportPersonnel.note: Treadgold, A History of the Byzantine State and Society (p. 277; via the Treadgold table at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byzantine_navy, pointer) estimates 30,000 oarsmen in 518 and 540 (mid). Low allows for Pryor and Jeffreys' smaller single-banked dromon crews; high adds staff and engineers.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Recruitment was voluntary plus barbarian federates; the state struggled to fill units after the plague (Jones, https://archive.org/details/JonesLaterRomanEmpire02, p. 684-685: Agathias' 150,000 field army for a huge area). 0.025 assumes an emergency levy roughly doubling the paid army.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Infantry ~75% of the 180,000-350,000 army (field armies about 1/3 cavalry, e.g. Belisarius' 10,000 foot + 5,000 horse in 533 (Procopius, ancient); limitanei mostly infantry; Elton 1996 pp. 105-106 puts late Roman cavalry at about 1/5 of effectives, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Roman_army, pointer). Line ~70% of infantry, the rest archers and light troops (Strategikon proportions of a generation later).

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: mail or lamellar, helmets, large shields, spears; well equipped from state fabricae.

training.note: Field-army infantry professional (0.75); limitanei part-time garrison soldiers (0.5).

count.note: Archer share of the infantry (~20%); see infantry_line for the arithmetic.
Educated guess. Javelinmen and skirmishers, Isaurian and Thracian light foot; ~10% of infantry.
Field-army cavalry (~1/3 of Agathias' 150,000 = ~50,000) less light allied horse: regiments of lancer-archers, bucellarii of the generals (Belisarius had some 7,000) and guards.

quality.note: Rubric 1.0: armoured lancer-archers with composite bows, the decisive arm of Belisarius and Narses; on a par with the savaran.

training.note: Long-service professionals and generals' household troops (rubric 0.75-1.0).

count.note: Hunnic, Herul and Moorish horse archers among the foederati in pay, plus limitanei cavalry units (cunei, equites) on the eastern and Danube frontiers.

quality.note: Steppe horse archers and light lancers (rubric 0.5-0.75).

training.note: Foederati professional but loosely disciplined; frontier units lower.

count.note: Educated guess. Ballistae and stone-throwers mounted on fortress and city walls (Procopius describes them at Rome in 537) and siege engines; Justinian built or rebuilt hundreds of forts (Procopius, Buildings). No count survives.

quality.note: Late Roman torsion artillery, still the era's best before the traction trebuchet arrived (c. 580s).

count.note: Educated guess. Single-banked dromons of ~50 oars; 92 dromons escorted the 533 Vandal expedition (Procopius, ancient). 30,000 oarsmen (Treadgold) divided over dromons and smaller craft.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: the dromon was the new standard war galley and the empire had no naval rival after 552 (Sena Gallica).

count.note: Educated guess. Danube flotilla, patrol and light craft; the transports of the expeditions (500 in 533) are merchant ships, not counted.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75: a trained staff hierarchy (magistri militum, duces) and proven commanders (Belisarius, Narses at Taginae 552 and Casilinum 554, John Troglita in Africa).

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5: regimental identity in the field units, but bucellarii loyal to their generals, mutinies over pay in Africa (536) and Italy, many barbarian federates.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: recent victories in Italy (552-554) and Spain (552), offset by plague losses, arrears of pay and the Lazic war.

weapons.note: Anchor 3 plus refinements: composite-bow lancer cavalry, torsion artillery; no traction trebuchet or crossbow yet.

armor.note: Anchor 3 exceeded: mail and lamellar standard, some horse armour; short of anchor 4 plate-and-mail.

ships.note: Anchor 3 plus the dromon (fully decked, lateen-rigged, single-banked); no Greek fire yet.

fortification.note: Above anchor 3: Theodosian land walls of Constantinople, Dara, the Anastasian Long Wall and Justinian's fort network; below anchor 4 concentric castles.

logistics.note: Anchor 3 plus state supply in kind (annona, coemptio) and seaborne transport supporting overseas expeditions.

communications.note: Anchor 3: cursus publicus, partly curtailed by Justinian (Procopius, Secret History 30).

isr.note: Year anchor 3: scouts (cursores), spies, frontier informants.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project Database 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true (2011 int$): year 1 CE Greece 1,275, Egypt/Levant/Tunisia 1,116, Turkey 897, Italy 1,407; Egypt 730 CE 1,164. The 6th-century East (Levant, Egypt, Asia Minor) was at a late-antique peak; Italy was devastated by the Gothic war. Mid ~1,000.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Army pay was the largest item of a budget Treadgold puts at a few million nomismata a year; land tax ~ a fifth to a quarter of output, of which the army took the largest part. Peacetime share; Justinian was also at war in Lazica in 555.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Agrarian economy; state fabricae, silk (sericulture introduced c. 552), mining, textiles, building programme.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Egypt still shipped ~8 million artabas of tax grain a year to Constantinople (Justinian Edict 13, ancient); surplus regions in Egypt, Africa and Sicily.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in an ancient Greek-type age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model used for all classical and medieval snapshots.

roadKm.note: ORBIS v1 (https://orbis.stanford.edu/orbis2012/ORBIS_v1paper_20120501.pdf) models 84,631 km of principal Roman roads and desert tracks c. 200 CE for the whole empire. The 555 empire held roughly 55-65% of that network (Balkans, Asia Minor, Levant, Egypt, Africa, Italy), less where roads had decayed (mid ~50,000 km).

majorPorts.note: ORBIS has 268 sea-port sites for the Roman Empire; ports able to supply a fleet or army in 555: Constantinople, Alexandria, Carthage, Ravenna, Syracuse, Thessalonica, Seleucia Pieria, Caesarea, Ephesus, Rhodes, Naples, Septem, Cartagena... estimated at ~15.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. The Egyptian grain fleet to Constantinople (~8 million artabas, ~200,000 t a year) plus Mediterranean trade; scaled below the rome-117 estimate for a smaller annona.

supplyRangeKm.note: By analogy with Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1): pre-modern armies with grain carried on soldiers and pack animals could operate ~1-2 weeks' march from a depot or navigable water; Justinian's expeditions moved by sea.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. ~0.075-0.11 draft and pack animals per inhabitant x population.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: fortified cities and fort networks, local supply and population support; Constantinople nearly impregnable. Recently conquered Italy and Africa gave less support.

notes: Snapshot = 555 CE, Justinian I after the end of the Gothic war (Casilinum 554) and the landing in Spain (552), with the Lazic war against Persia still running (551-557). Force convention: activePersonnel = comitatenses, foederati and bucellarii in imperial pay, limitanei, guards and fleet; allied contingents (Lombards, Heruls, Ghassanids) in trainedReserves. Agathias' 150,000 (contemporary, end of the reign) and his 645,000 for the "old days" are ancient figures; the mid follows Treadgold for structure and Jones for the reading of Agathias. Treadgold's two books are cited by ISBN (not fetchable); his numbers were read from Wikipedia tables (pointer only), so they are graded B at most. Border = historical-basemaps world_500 Eastern Roman Empire + Vandals + Ostrogoths polygons (the nearest file before 555 shows the pre-reconquest empire); this includes Provence and Raetia (not recovered) and misses the Spanish strip. Population inside the border after the first plague wave of 541-542.
